issue_context.title: MIN and MAX attributes in Angular 12 templated forms not working with decimal values
issue_context.body:
# Bug Report

### Affected Package

FormsModule
@angular/forms

Commit: 8fb83ea1b524663bd804908308d528c338450270
* feat(forms): introduce min and max validators (#39063)

validators.ts:

Using parseInt rather than parsefloat ?

```
normalizeInput = (input: string): number => parseInt(input, 10);
```

### Is this a regression?

MIN/MAX attributes didn't participate in templated forms validity < v12 so not a regression as such.

### Description

MIN and MAX attributes not honouring decimal values in v12. In the example below, the form becomes invalid with a maximum over 37, e.g. 37.1 makes form invalid when it should be > 37.5

```html
<form #someform="ngForm">
  <input
    [(ngModel)]="model.formContractHours"
    required
    name="ContractHours"
    type="number"
    [min]="0.1"
    [max]="37.5"
    step="0.1"
  />
</form>
```
## Minimal Reproduction

MIN/MAX attributes ignored in V11 templated form
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular11minmaxdecimals

MIN/MAX attributes validated in V12 in templated form but not respecting decimals.
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular12minmaxdecimals

review_comments: The tests added in this PR verify the logic of the underlying `Validators.min` and `Validators.max` validator functions, but they are not checking the behavior of the min/max validator directives that was actually changed. These tests are actually helpful and we should keep them (I didn't find existing tests that verify the logic with float numbers) + we should add tests to verify directives logic as well. You can look at the test cases added in the original PR #39063 (see `packages/forms/test/template_integration_spec.ts` and `packages/forms/test/reactive_integration_spec.ts`) and either update them with additional cases or create a couple new ones. Please let me know if you have any questions, will be happy to help. Thank you.

@AndrewKushnir  thanks, that was really good input. While writing test case I realize that still input wasn't allowing float number, so I did code change for it as well. Feel free to provide any other inputs as well.
